themes: Clients ask for AI productivity at renewal and now mid-contract; Infosys calls it 'AI-led deflation' on large and small deals but does not quantify it (Jul-2026). Kotak assumes 3-3.5% a year of GenAI deflation for incumbents (Jul-2026). It is why FY26 volumes were flat and FY27 organic growth is ~0.5%.

AI-first services 8.2% of Infosys revenue in Q1FY27 (5.5% in Q3FY26); 80,000 staff on AI coding tools; Topaz Fabric runs 15 models. Management compares it with digital, which went from 20% to 60% of revenue in a few years, but gives no target.
20% of Infosys's Q1FY27 large-deal TCV came from consolidation wins (US$700 mn net new). Clients cutting costs move work to fewer, larger suppliers.

European auto and manufacturing weak; tariffs, the Middle East conflict and oil above US$90 keep budgets tight; US rate-hike fears returned in Sep-2026. Retail and communications clients most cautious.
Clients build their own captive centres in India (some work insourced) but also hire vendors to set up and run them; Infosys says its GCC work is growing but gives no number.
AI labs and hyperscalers building services arms
AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are adding forward-deployed engineers; Infosys sees them as partners for now (Jul-2026).

From 9-Sep-2026 employers pay US$4,000 per H-1B and US$4,500 per L-1 extension; the US suspended Cognizant's labour-certification filings; the DOJ is investigating Infosys's H-1B classification for one client. Onsite effort is already down to 22.8%.
Rs/US$ 95.8 on 30-Sep-2026 vs 88.6 average in FY26; each 1% adds 15-17 bp to Infosys's margin, partly reinvested and partly offset by weaker client currencies.

structural: Infosys's FY26 volumes were flat; growth came from price (Project Maximus). Q1FY27 organic revenue fell 0.1% QoQ and organic FY27 guidance is ~0.5% at the midpoint (Jul-2026).
Management now names 'AI-led deflation' on renewals and mid-contract, across verticals (CFO and CEO, Jul-2026).
Headcount was flat for two years (323,578 Mar-25, 328,062 Jun-26) while US$ revenue rose ~5%: the work needs fewer people.

Kotak raised its GenAI deflation assumption to 3-3.5% a year and its cost of equity for disruption risk; it sees no re-rating without faster growth or AI value-capture pricing (Jul-2026). Nirmal Bang: the guidance cut 'could just be the beginning'.
The sell-off started with a global rout in software and outsourcing stocks after a new Anthropic AI tool (Feb-2026), not with an earnings miss.
cyclical: Large-deal TCV kept growing: US$14.7 bn in the twelve months to Jun-26, +30% YoY (Anand Rathi), 61% net new in Q1FY27.
Margins held at ~21% and FCF stayed above 100% of profit; a weak rupee helps.
Part of the FY27 cut is client-specific (an EURS programme termination, a European manufacturer) and macro (European auto, tariffs), which can reverse.
AI services grew from 5.5% to 8.2% of revenue in two quarters.
sectorQuestion.verdict: Mostly lasting. The cyclical parts are real but the business has shifted from volume growth to price-led, near-zero organic growth, and the company itself says AI deflation is now part of every renewal. We do not assume the multiple returns to its 2021-25 range: we apply the IT sector's median de-rating to Infosys's own history.

moat: 41 clients pay >US$100 mn a year and 333 >US$10 mn; top-25 clients 33.9% of revenue; decades-long relationships and 20% of Q1FY27 TCV from consolidation wins.
Keeps the work coming, but clients now use AI productivity to reprice it at every renewal.
328,000 people, 77% of effort offshore, utilisation ~85%. Labour arbitrage built the industry; AI coding tools make the same work need fewer people, so scale in headcount matters less.
The cost advantage over Western rivals remains; over AI-native delivery it is shrinking.
Leader ratings in many analyst assessments (Gartner, Everest, HFS); a top-3 Indian IT brand; history of governance disputes (2017, 2019) now settled.
Wins shortlists; does not command a price premium.
Finacle banking software and the Topaz/Topaz Fabric AI platform; but >95% of revenue is services billed by effort or outcome.
No product moat; AI platforms are partner-dependent (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft).
EBIT ~21% for five years through a boom, a bust and wage inflation; FCF >100% of profit; debt-free; ROE ~31%.
Shows pricing discipline (it walks away from uneconomic deals) and protects the dividend.
Project Maximus delivered price gains in a flat-volume year; but growth has lagged TCS in some years and the CEO hands over in Apr-2027 in the middle of the AI shift.
critiques: AI deflation is just starting: guidance cuts will continue as more contracts renew at AI-productivity prices
Organic growth visibility is poor (~0.5% at the FY27 midpoint) and there are few near-term catalysts
The CEO transition (Apr-2027) may weigh; Infosys may underperform peers near term
The guidance is conservative, deal wins are strong and AI revenue is scaling; 12.6x FY28E is cheap
12x FY28E EPS and a ~6% payout yield (dividends plus buybacks) limit the downside
The miss was client-specific and margins beat
A re-rating needs faster growth or pricing that captures AI value; neither is visible

gaps: The company does not quantify AI-led deflation or say how much of its contract base has been repriced.
Vertical (segment) margins are disclosed annually in the AR but not modelled; we model one margin.
Upfront cash paid for Optimum and Stratus is not disclosed separately in what we read; we use the US$466 mn rise in goodwill and intangibles in Q1FY27 (~Rs4,400 cr) as the proxy.
Whether the Versent (Telstra) deal closed by 30-Sep-2026 is not confirmed; we exclude it.
The status of the 2024 GST notice on overseas-branch services could not be verified in sources to 30-Sep-2026; it is not in the FY26 contingent liabilities, and GST disputes in the AR total Rs326 cr.
Size of the Oct-2026/Jan-2027 wage hikes not disclosed.
Net-new share of large-deal TCV for Q3FY26 and Q4FY26 not collected.
Motilal Oswal, Choice and 360 ONE FY28E EPS not available; implied from target / multiple.
No post-results Kotak note found; its 3-Jul-2026 fair value is pre-results.
Average Rs/US$ for Q2FY27 not collected; we assume ~95.6 (Q1 94.9; 30-Sep spot 95.81).
Named shareholders at Jun-2026 are from Trendlyne (aggregator of the BSE filing), not the filing itself.
The web-search budget ran out during research; a few items (2024 GST notice, 2023 McCamish cyber incident) were not re-checked.
An Arihant Capital note (13-Aug-2026; BUY, Rs1,421 on 14x FY29E EPS per a search snippet) was not opened or verified and is left out of the street table.
conflicts: FY26 EPS: Screener Rs72.59 (year-end 405.6 cr shares) vs reported basic Rs71.58 (weighted 411.3 cr shares, buyback in December). We use Screener's basis because the forecast share count is the year-end count.

Motilal Oswal target: Rs1,170 (Business Today, Trendlyne) vs Rs1,550 on one aggregator page (stale); we use Rs1,170.
